name: Jabesh Gilead
overview: Jabesh Gilead was a city east of the Jordan River that notably failed to join the assembly at Mizpeh, prompting a severe judgment from the tribes of Israel. As recorded in Judges 21, twelve thousand valiant men were sent to strike the inhabitants, sparing only four hundred young virgins who had not known a man, and these women were brought to Shiloh. This account highlights the city's isolation and the consequences of its absence from Israel's covenantal gathering, underscoring the seriousness of communal faithfulness and obedience in the Old Testament context.
